title: Pluricanonical linear systems on stable geometric curves
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $C/K$ be an unpointed stable curve of arithmetic genus $g\geq2$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], with dualizing line $\omega_C$ [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing]. For every integer $n\geq3$, the line $\omega_C^{\otimes n}$ is very ample: its evaluation morphism is a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_K(H^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes n}))$ in the convention of one-dimensional quotients [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. One has $\deg\omega_C=2g-2$, $H^q(C,\omega_C^{\otimes n})=0$ for $q>0$, and $\dim_K H^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes n})=(2n-1)(g-1)$. For every integer $m$ one has $\chi(C,\omega_C^{\otimes nm})=n(2g-2)m+1-g$, where $\chi$ is the alternating sum of coherent-cohomology dimensions [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. The degree is [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], and $H^q$ denotes Zariski sheaf cohomology [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. These conclusions hold for reducible and singular stable curves, and after arbitrary field extension.

source.place: Tag 0E8X, lemma-tricanonical (very ampleness for n=3), Tag 0BS6, lemma-rr, and Tag 0E3E, lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein; general n>=3 uses the same length-two-subscheme argument as 0E8X. Morrison Section 3.3, preceding Definition 9, also records n>=3; its PDF is locally WANTED.

proof.text: First work over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Unpack the unpointed stable genus-$g$ hypothesis: $C$ is nonempty, connected, reduced, nodal and pure of dimension one, flat and finitely presented over $\Omega$, and projective in the projective-bundle convention. Thus $C$ is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. The spectrum of a field has one point and has Noetherian coordinate ring (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so it is a Noetherian scheme. Finite presentation implies finite type; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] therefore makes $C$ Noetherian. Invertible modules are quasi-coherent and locally generated by one element, hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Proper coherent cohomology is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined], and cohomology above degree one vanishes by [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension]. Finally [lem-sc-global-functions] gives $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=\Omega$, and the genus hypothesis gives $h^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=g$.

source.place: Tag 0E8X, geometric-field reduction; varieties.tex, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections; coherent.tex Tags 01XZ and 02O5; cohomology.tex Tag 02UZ

proof.text: The line $\omega_C$ is the relative dualizing line for $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-nodal-dualizing-base-change] to this proper flat finitely presented nodal family. It supplies precisely the nodal dualizing datum required in [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-field-linear-series], and on each normalized component $V$ gives $\deg(\nu^*\omega_C)=2g(V)-2+b_V$, with $b_V$ counting both branches of a self-node. By stability this integer is positive: when $g(V)=0$ there are at least three branches; when $g(V)=1$ there is at least one; when $g(V)\geq2$ the term $2g(V)-2$ is already positive. Thus all component-degree hypotheses of that field-linear-series theorem hold with $r=0$, empty marking divisor $D=0$, and $M=\omega_C\otimes\mathcal O_C(0)=\omega_C$. The last equality is the zero-divisor instance of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].

source.place: Tag 0E6R and preceding relative-dualizing discussion; duality.tex Tags 0E9Y and 0E9Z for the nodal adjunction comparison; curves.tex Tag 0C4D

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-field-linear-series] to the data verified in step 2. For every $n\geq3$ it gives $H^q(C,\omega_C^{\otimes n})=0$ for every $q>0$, global generation, and a closed immersion given by the complete linear system into the projective space of one-dimensional quotients of $H^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes n})$. This is the evaluation morphism in the one-dimensional-quotient convention: [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] characterizes a map to this projective space by its quotient $H^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes n})\otimes_\Omega\mathcal O_C\twoheadrightarrow\omega_C^{\otimes n}$. In particular its tautological line pulls back to $\omega_C^{\otimes n}$. Only the positive-degree, unmarked specialization of the existing theorem is used; neither its normal-generation clause nor any contraction assertion is needed.

source.place: Section 1, Theorem 1.8 and Corollary 1.9, positive-degree case with no markings; used as the statement of the existing DAG prerequisite, whose local PDF is WANTED

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing] to the structure morphism $f:C\to T=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. It gives that $\omega_C$ is invertible and $f^!\mathcal O_T\simeq\omega_C[1]$, where $f^!$ is right adjoint to the derived direct image $Rf_*$ on derived quasi-coherent modules [def-pc-derived-category]. For a quasi-coherent $F$ on $C$, placed in degree $0$, Hom between modules in degree $0$ is Hom in the derived category, so $\operatorname{Hom}_C(F,\omega_C)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_C)}(F,f^!\mathcal O_T[-1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Omega)}(Rf_*F,\Omega[-1])$. A complex of $\Omega$-vector spaces is isomorphic to the sum of its shifted cohomology spaces, and $H^i(Rf_*F)=H^i(C,F)$ over the affine base [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]; hence the right side is $\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(H^1(C,F),\Omega)$. Take $F=\mathcal O_C$ and $F=\omega_C$. The first Hom is $H^0(C,\omega_C)$, while $\operatorname{Hom}_C(\omega_C,\omega_C)=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$: in a local basis an endomorphism of a line is multiplication by a function, and these functions agree on overlaps. Finite-dimensionality from step 1 now gives $h^0(C,\omega_C)=g$ and $h^1(C,\omega_C)=1$. Together with vanishing above degree one, $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-g$ and $\chi(C,\omega_C)=g-1$ (the numerical form of Stacks Tag 0BS5). The definition [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] therefore gives $\deg\omega_C=(g-1)-(1-g)=2g-2$.

source.place: Tag 0BS5 (lemma-euler) and Tag 0BS6 (lemma-rr); moduli-curves.tex Tag 0E6R (lemma-gorenstein-dualizing) and the preceding description of the relative dualizing module via the right adjoint of derived direct image

proof.text: For every integer $a$, the tensor-degree theorem [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive] gives $\deg(\omega_C^{\otimes a})=a\deg\omega_C$. For $a\geq0$ this is induction starting with $\deg\mathcal O_C=0$. For negative $a$, use the invertible dual and evaluation isomorphism $\omega_C\otimes\omega_C^\vee\cong\mathcal O_C$ from [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible], so $\deg\omega_C^\vee=-\deg\omega_C$, and apply the same induction. These modules and tensor products are invertible by that same node. Substitution into [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] yields $\chi(C,\omega_C^{\otimes a})=a(2g-2)+1-g$ for all integers $a$. Taking $a=nm$ proves the asserted formula for every integer $m$, including $m=0$ and negative $m$. Taking $a=n\geq3$ and using the higher-cohomology vanishing in step 3 gives $h^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes n})=n(2g-2)+1-g=(2n-1)(g-1)$.

source.place: Tag 0BS6, rank-one numerical formula; varieties.tex Tag 0AYX (lemma-degree-tensor-product) and degree definition Tag 0AYR

proof.text: Over arbitrary $K$, projectivity gives properness by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], and finite presentation gives finite type. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/K$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The pullback family is again a stable genus-$g$ curve: the moduli-groupoid definition specifies pullback by fibre product and imposes the same genus on every geometric fibre. The relative-dualizing base-change theorem identifies its dualizing line with the pullback of $\omega_C$; [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] identifies the positive tensor powers, and the dual/evaluation identities identify negative powers as well, since the pullback of an inverse line is again an inverse of the pulled-back line. All these lines are quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]. The field extension is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat], so [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] gives $H^q(C_\Omega,F_\Omega)\cong H^q(C,F)\otimes_K\Omega$ for each of the line bundles and for $F=\mathcal O_C$. For a $K$-basis indexed by $I$, tensoring its direct-sum decomposition gives an $\Omega$-basis indexed by the same $I$. Hence finiteness, dimension and vanishing are reflected. Applying this in every degree also reflects finite cohomological support and the Euler sum, including for negative powers. The geometric very ampleness descends by [lem-pc-very-ample-descends], which applies because $C$ is of finite type. Here very ample has the complete-linear-system meaning of [def-sc-ample]; the quotient universal property identifies that morphism with the evaluation quotient in the one-dimensional-quotient convention. Degree is unchanged by [lem-pc-degree-base-change]. This proves all assertions over $K$. For any further field extension $K'/K$, apply the same argument to the pulled-back stable family, with the same genus and dualizing line by the cited base-change theorem. No smoothness or irreducibility was used.
